scenes.text: It's Friday afternoon. An engineer picks up a ticket: add session replay to the payslip screen, using a vendor called Glimpse. It looks routine. It isn't. In this sample company, forty enterprise customers were promised sixty days' written notice before any new subprocessor touches their payroll data. Nobody told legal. And moving the ticket to Done takes one click.

That's the gap. Privacy counsel sign the contracts. Engineers close the tickets. The knowledge needed to stop this exists, but it lives in two different tools. Aviso Previo connects them, inside Jira and Confluence.

Counsel start in the admin workspace. Every contract is a Confluence page. Claude reads it, and the app shows the extracted terms right beside the clause as signed. If the model quotes anything that isn't in the contract, word for word, it's rejected. And when the wording is vague, like a reasonable period, nothing is guessed. It's marked: counsel to decide. A person resolves it. Not the model.

Now the engineer's side. On the Glimpse ticket, the Aviso Previo panel shows a release hold. Forty confirmed contracts apply. The longest notice is sixty days, so the earliest permitted go-live is the nineteenth of January. That date is calculated in code, never by the model.

When the engineer tries to move the ticket to Done, Jira refuses, and says exactly why. Counsel can override, with a written reason that's recorded. A ticket that says synthetic data only still needs a person to confirm it. And if a ticket can't be read, or no contracts are confirmed, the release stays blocked. It fails closed.

Does the model read contracts correctly? We measured it. Claude read all forty-one contracts from Confluence, and every answer was scored against a label. The first run declined twelve of them: the sample clauses never said calendar or business days, so the model refused to guess. We fixed the text and ran it again. Forty-one out of forty-one, and zero confident wrong answers. It's our own sample set, so it shows behaviour, not general accuracy. But the behaviour is the point: quote it, or say you can't.

Teams can also just ask. The Aviso Previo agent in Rovo, and the same tools over M C P, answer from the register: what adding Glimpse commits you to, or what a clause says. Ask about the ambiguous one, and it says counsel must decide. And every contract is added to the Teamwork Graph, so contracts and work can finally live in one graph.
Aviso Previo. Built on Forge, for privacy counsel, and the engineers who ship. Ship on the date your contracts allow.
